examples.title: Basic
examples.description: A bounded whole number with a unit. Keep the number in state and update it from `onValueChange`. Give the field an `aria-label`: the steppers are named after it.

examples.title: Hours and minutes
examples.description: Two fields side by side make a delay. Each keeps its own limits; a step turns the digits like an odometer.

examples.title: Typing above a minimum
examples.description: Typing keeps a draft. A number inside the limits applies at once; one below the minimum is held while you type, so 25 can be typed above a minimum of 10. It is clamped when you leave the field or press Enter, and Escape puts the old value back.

examples.title: Negative numbers
examples.description: Set `min` below zero and the field accepts a minus sign. With a minimum of zero or more it is refused.

examples.title: Step and large step
examples.description: `step` is how far a chevron or an arrow key moves, from a grid that starts at `min`. `largeStep` (ten steps by default) is how far PageUp, PageDown and Shift+Arrow move.

examples.title: No maximum
examples.description: Without `max` the field has no upper limit, and a new place opens its width as the number gains a digit. A function of the value can pick the suffix.

examples.title: Without a suffix
examples.description: `suffix` is optional. Leave it out for a bare number.

examples.title: Error
examples.description: `state="error"` turns the border red and sets `aria-invalid`. Describe the problem in a message and link it with `aria-describedby`.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.description: A disabled field dims on a grey surface; the input and both steppers leave the interaction.

examples.title: Stepper labels
examples.description: By default the steppers read "Increase <aria-label>" and "Decrease <aria-label>". `incrementAriaLabel` and `decrementAriaLabel` say it in your own words.

examples.title: Keyboard
examples.description: The input answers the arrow, page, Home and End keys, so the chevrons are not Tab stops. At a limit a press strains the value, and the limit is announced politely.
